title: Reading Drill — Counting seats at outdoor events — Reviewing the evidence
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Counting seats at outdoor events — Reviewing the evidence
passages.body:
**A** The event safety team in Cairnford received an old report about spectators standing near exits despite visible seats. The report compared the number of people beside the exits, but some entries had been collected under different conditions. To check the report, reviewers returned to the overhead photographs rather than treating the published figures as a complete record.

**B** The review covered three weeks. In the first part of that period, the original records did not consistently include temporary rain showers. In the later part, the recording sheet included a separate field for it. The reviewers kept readings from both periods, but marked which items were missing rather than guessing what had happened.

**C** The conclusion listed an usher near the spare seats as a possible later response. It recommended collecting another set of readings before deciding whether to use it. The new data would be published with the method, so another group could work out whether its own measurements were comparable.
